options.text: The determinant 8 is right, but uniqueness also requires the constants to be positive numbers.

options.text: The determinant of that matrix is 2 times 2 minus 4 times 1, which is 0, so there is no unique solution.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a determinant decides uniqueness of a solution.
questions.stem: A biologist has to determine whether a two-equation survey system has a unique solution. Explain how the determinant of the coefficient matrix answers that question.

answer.exemplar: For a system with coefficient matrix [[a,b],[c,d]] the determinant is ad - bc. If it is nonzero, the rows are independent, the system has exactly one solution for any right-hand side, and the surveyor can trust the answer. If the determinant is zero, the rows are multiples of one another, so the system either has no solution or infinitely many, and the surveyor must look at the constants to decide which case holds.

questions.explanation: A nonzero determinant means the rows are independent, so the system has exactly one solution. A zero determinant means dependent rows, giving either no solution or infinitely many, decided by the constants.
questions.hint: Zero determinant means dependent rows.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Explain how row reduction classifies a system.
questions.stem: A biologist has a survey system in augmented matrix form and wants to know whether it can be solved uniquely. Describe how row reduction reveals the answer.

answer.exemplar: Reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. If every row has a pivot and there are pivots in as many columns as unknowns, the system has a unique solution and the last column gives the values after back-substitution. If a row reduces to 0x + 0y = 5, the equations contradict each other and there is no solution. If a row reduces to 0x + 0y = 0, one equation is redundant, leaving a free variable and infinitely many solutions.

questions.explanation: Pivots and zero rows separate the cases: pivots everywhere means unique, a zero row with a nonzero constant means no solution, a zero row with zero constant means infinitely many.
questions.hint: Read the pivots and any zero row.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Set up a system for a survey with an overlapping count.
questions.stem: A biologist surveys two plots and knows the totals of two plant species plus the count of plots holding both. Explain how to write and solve the system that answers the survey question.

answer.exemplar: Let a be the number of plots with only species one and b the number with only species two, so the totals become a + c and b + c, where c is the number of plots holding both. Write the two equations a + c = p and b + c = q, then subtract c from each to get the exclusive counts. Alternatively use the count of plots with at least one species, d, and solve a + b + c = d together with the two totals for a, b and c by elimination.

questions.explanation: A variable for the shared case keeps the totals honest, since the overlap must come out of both totals. Elimination then isolates the exclusive counts, and the unique solution answers the question.
questions.hint: Give the overlap its own variable.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Describe a three by three determinant expansion and its signs.
questions.stem: A biologist wants to compute the determinant of a 3 by 3 survey matrix. Explain the method and why the signs alternate.

answer.exemplar: Expand along a row or column of the 3 by 3 matrix, forming three 2 by 2 minors. The signs follow the checkerboard pattern plus, minus, plus, minus, plus, minus across the chosen row, so the expansion reads a(ei - fh) - b(di - fg) + c(dh - eg) for the rows a b c, d e f and g h i. Each minor is itself a determinant computed as the product of one diagonal minus the product of the other, and the alternating signs keep the value consistent with the way rows and columns are ordered.

questions.explanation: A three by three determinant is built from three two by two minors with alternating signs, and each minor subtracts one diagonal product from the other. The signs encode entry order, so dropping them changes the value.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why a homogeneous system always has the trivial solution.
questions.stem: A biologist asks why a homogeneous survey system always has the trivial solution. Explain the reason.

answer.exemplar: In a homogeneous system every equation reads zero on the right-hand side, so the all-zero triple satisfies every equation at once and is always a solution. questions.stem: A biologist's system has coefficient matrix [[8,3],[5,2]]. Using the two by two determinant formula, what is the determinant?
questions.explanation: The determinant is ad - bc = 8(2) - 3(5) = 1. Because it is nonzero, the survey system has a unique solution, and adding the products instead would give 31.
questions.hint: Multiply the diagonals and subtract.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Solve a survey ratio problem with a total.
questions.stem: A biologist's water samples contain a fixed number of organisms and the count of one species is three times the count of the other, with a total of 48. How many organisms belong to the more numerous species?
questions.explanation: Writing the counts as s and 3s gives 4s = 48, so s = 12 and the more numerous species has 36 organisms. Reading the ratio as 2 to 1 would give 32, which does not fit the total.
questions.hint: Express both counts from the smaller one.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Solve a homogeneous system and identify its only solution.
questions.stem: A biologist's survey notes give the homogeneous system 2x - y = 0 and x + 3y = 0. What is the value of y in its solution, in units?
questions.explanation: The first equation gives y = 2x; substituting into the second gives 7x = 0, so x = 0 and y = 0. The determinant is 7, nonzero, so the trivial solution is the only one.
questions.hint: Eliminate one unknown entirely.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Predict the effect of a row swap on a determinant.
questions.stem: A biologist swaps two rows of a 2 by 2 coefficient matrix and computes the determinant again. What happens to the value?

options.text: The determinant is unchanged, because row order does not affect the products in the formula.
options.misconception: believes row order never changes a determinant

options.text: The determinant doubles, because the matrix now spans twice the area of the plane.
options.misconception: believes a row swap doubles the determinant

options.text: The determinant becomes zero, because the swapped rows can no longer be reduced by row operations.
options.misconception: believes swapping rows destroys independence

options.text: The determinant changes sign, because a single row swap reverses the orientation of the parallelogram.

questions.explanation: A single row swap multiplies the determinant by -1, so its sign flips while the magnitude is unchanged. Swapping two rows would cancel out, and row order never affects independence.
questions.hint: One swap reverses the sign.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Weigh the evidence a zero determinant gives about a system.
questions.stem: A biologist says a system with coefficient matrix [[1,2],[2,4]] has infinitely many solutions. What evidence supports or contradicts that claim?

options.text: The determinant is 1 times 4 minus 2 times 2, which is 0, so the rows are dependent and the claim is consistent.
options.misconception: believes a zero determinant guarantees infinitely many solutions

options.text: The determinant is 1 times 4 minus 2 times 2, which is 0, so the rows are dependent but the constants decide the case.
The determinant is 1 times 4 plus 2 times 2, which is 8, so the rows are independent and the claim is false.
options.misconception: believes the determinant formula adds the products

options.text: The determinant is 1 times 4 minus 2 times 2, which is 0, so the system has no solution and the claim is false.
options.misconception: believes a zero determinant guarantees no solution

questions.explanation: A zero determinant means dependent rows, which rules out a unique solution but leaves open either none or infinitely many. Only the constants and the reduced form separate those two cases.
questions.hint: A zero determinant alone is not enough.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Interpret a reduction of an overdetermined survey system.
questions.stem: A biologist has a survey question with two unknowns and three independent equations. Explain what happens when the system is reduced and what the biologist should conclude.

answer.exemplar: Reduce the three equations by elimination and watch the pattern of pivots. Two independent pivots leave a third row that reduces to 0x + 0y = c. If c is not zero, the three equations cannot all hold, so at least one measurement is wrong and the biologist should recheck the data. If c is zero, the third equation is redundant, which is common in survey work where one site was recorded twice, and the first two equations give the unique answer.

questions.explanation: Three equations for two unknowns leave one pivot-free row after reduction. A nonzero constant there means the data are inconsistent, while a zero constant means the extra equation is redundant.
questions.hint: Look at the row left without a pivot.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Apply a row replacement and read one entry of the result.
questions.stem: A biologist replaces the row [3, 6, 1] by that row minus 4 times the row [1, 1, 2]. What is the second entry of the new row?
questions.explanation: Four times the second row is [4, 4, 8], and subtracting it from [3, 6, 1] gives [-1, 2, -7], whose second entry is 2. Adding the rows without the factor of 4 would give 7 for that entry instead.
questions.hint: Scale the second row before subtracting.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Expand a three by three determinant along its first row.
questions.stem: A biologist uses a cofactor expansion on [[2,0,1],[0,3,4],[1,5,6]] along its first row. What value does the expansion give?
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row gives 2 times (18 - 20) plus 1 times (0 - 3), which is -4 - 3 = -7. The middle term vanishes because its coefficient is zero, and dropping the plus on the third term would give -1.
questions.hint: Keep the plus and minus signs in the expansion.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: State what a zero determinant implies for a homogeneous system.
questions.stem: A biologist solves a homogeneous system with two unknowns and finds the determinant of the coefficient matrix is 0. What must be true?

options.text: The system has infinitely many solutions, so some nonzero pairs also satisfy both equations.
The system has a unique solution, and that solution must be the all-zero triple.
options.misconception: believes a zero determinant still isolates one solution

options.text: The system has no solution, because dependent rows cannot satisfy both equations at once.
options.misconception: believes dependent rows force a contradiction

options.text: The system has exactly one nonzero solution, since the zero triple is already known.
options.misconception: believes homogeneity leaves exactly one free pair

questions.explanation: A zero determinant means dependent rows, so one equation repeats the other and nonzero pairs satisfy both equations. The zero triple is always present, but it is not the only solution.
questions.hint: Dependent rows leave a free choice.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Detect a wrong determinant claimed from a triangular matrix.
questions.stem: A biologist puts a survey matrix into triangular form, giving [[1,0,2],[0,1,-1],[0,0,0]], and claims the determinant is 1. What is the error in the claim?

options.text: The determinant is the product of the diagonal, which is 1 times 1 times 0, so the correct value is 0.
options.misconception: believes the zero on the diagonal should be ignored

options.text: The determinant is 1 times 1 times 0, which is 0, so the claim of 1 is correct after rounding.
options.misconception: believes a zero diagonal product can be rounded up

options.text: The determinant is -2, because the entry 2 in the first row contributes to the value.
options.misconception: believes entries above pivots change the determinant

options.text: The determinant is 0, because a zero row means the matrix is singular, so the claim of 1 is wrong.

questions.explanation: The diagonal product is 1 times 1 times 0, which is 0, and a zero row confirms the matrix is singular. Counting only the two nonzero pivots and ignoring the zero would wrongly give 1.
questions.hint: Multiply all three diagonal entries.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Describe reduced row echelon form and its usefulness.
questions.stem: A biologist wants to move from a survey matrix to reduced row echelon form. Describe what that form looks like and why it is useful.

answer.exemplar: Reduced row echelon form has a leading 1 in each pivot column, every other entry in that column equal to zero, and each pivot strictly to the right of the one above it. When the coefficient block becomes the identity matrix, each unknown is read directly from the last column, so the survey counts need no back-substitution. The reduction preserves the solution set at every step, because row replacements, scalings and swaps leave the set of satisfying triples unchanged.

questions.explanation: Reduced row echelon form isolates each unknown in its own column with zeros elsewhere, so the answers sit in the last column. Reaching it changes only how the rows are written, never which triples satisfy the system.
questions.hint: Identity on the left, answers on the right.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Correct a claim that a dependent homogeneous system has one solution.
questions.stem: A biologist claims the homogeneous system 3x + 2y = 0 and 6x + 4y = 0 has only the trivial solution. What is the error in the claim?

options.text: The system is consistent, so the claim is right, but the determinant should have been computed before deciding.
options.misconception: believes consistency settles the number of solutions

options.text: The rows are proportional, so any nonzero pair on the line satisfies both equations, giving infinitely many solutions.
The second equation should have been reduced to 0x + 0y = 0, which would show that only the zero triple works.
options.misconception: believes a zero row forces the trivial solution

options.text: The determinant of the coefficient matrix is 3 times 4 minus 2 times 6, which is 0, so the claim is correct.
options.misconception: believes a zero determinant proves uniqueness of the trivial solution

questions.explanation: The second row is twice the first, so the unknowns satisfy only one condition and infinitely many pairs work. A zero determinant signals dependence, not a unique solution.
questions.hint: Check whether one row is a multiple.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Explain a system with independent rows but conflicting constants.
questions.stem: A biologist's survey system has a nonzero determinant but the constants make the equations disagree. Explain what that combination means.

answer.exemplar: A nonzero determinant says the coefficient rows are independent, so the two equations are not multiples of one another and each contributes independent information. Even so, the pairs of counts that satisfy each equation separately can be different, and no single pair lies on both lines at once. That is the definition of an inconsistent system: the coefficients are perfectly well behaved, but the constants place the two lines in positions where they never meet, so the survey data must contain an error.

questions.explanation: The determinant describes the coefficient rows, not whether the constants agree. Independent rows with conflicting constants give parallel lines that never meet, so no solution exists.
questions.hint: The determinant ignores the constants.

questions.learningObjective: Choose the row operation that clears an entry below a pivot.
questions.stem: A biologist must clear the entry below a pivot of 5 when that entry is 20. Which row operation does this, and what is the result?

options.text: Replace the lower row by itself minus 4 times the pivot row, which removes the entry 20 below 5.
options.misconception: believes the multiplier must be 20 divided by 5 twice

options.text: Replace the lower row by itself plus 4 times the pivot row, which removes the entry 20 below 5.
options.misconception: believes adding clears an entry below a pivot

options.text: Scale the lower row by 5 and then 4, which removes the entry 20 below 5.
options.misconception: believes scaling can clear an entry below a pivot

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Correct a part computed by adding instead of subtracting.
questions.stem: A biologist knows the sightings in habitats one and two together total 34, and that habitat one alone has 19 sightings. The biologist reports 53 for habitat two. What is the error?

options.text: Habitat two must be found by subtracting, so 34 - 19 = 15, and adding the two figures gives the wrong answer.
Habitat two must be found by dividing, so 34 divided by 19 gives the count of sightings there.
options.misconception: believes a part is found by dividing the total by one part

options.text: The figures are consistent, because 19 and 53 can both be part of a total of 34 sightings.
options.misconception: believes a part may exceed the total it belongs to

options.text: The total should have been 72, since habitat two must contain more sightings than habitat one.
options.misconception: believes the larger habitat must hold the larger count

questions.explanation: The part is the total minus the known part, so 34 - 19 = 15 sightings lie in habitat two. Adding the figures treats the known part as extra, and no part can exceed the total.
questions.hint: A part equals the total minus the rest.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a determinant decides whether counts can satisfy two equations.
questions.stem: A biologist wants to know whether two survey equations can both be satisfied by one set of counts. Explain how the determinant answers that question.

answer.exemplar: Put the coefficients of the two counts into a two by two matrix, say [[a,b],[c,d]], and compute ad - bc. If this value is not zero, the two rows are not multiples of one another, so they describe genuinely different conditions and exactly one pair of counts satisfies both. If the value is zero, the second equation is a multiple of the first, so the equations either agree for many count pairs or disagree entirely, and the constants decide which.

questions.explanation: A nonzero determinant means the rows are not multiples, so one count pair satisfies both conditions. A zero determinant makes them dependent, and the constants then decide between none and infinitely many.
questions.hint: Zero determinant means dependent rows.
